reason: Generic unexplained fee on the account; nothing says it was a card-payment fee, so card_payment_fee_charged assumes context not in the text.
Asks whether the account is usable before verification (the dataset's why_verify_identity sense), but 'not been accepted yet' also reads as a verification problem.
A one-off payment to an unrecognised seller is a card payment; no direct debit is mentioned.
Pure how-long question about transfer clearing; no claim that a balance failed to update.
Complaint is about ATM withdrawal charges; exchange rate is never mentioned.
Recipient got less than sent, which the dataset attributes to a deducted fee, but the text names no fee and jev's not-received label also half-fits.
'Not working' reads as a failed top-up, though 'had some money... not sure what happened' could hint at a reversal.
Card was declined at a restaurant payment; that is the declined_card_payment intent, not generic card_not_working.
Asks about top-up fees with no method given; neither bank-transfer nor card fee label is supported by the text.
Transfer could not be made; no beneficiary restriction is mentioned.
Asks whether the top-up is not working; nothing indicates it is pending.
Asks how to order a new card; expiry is never mentioned.
Changing/exchanging currency is exchange_via_app; fiat_currency_support is about which currencies are supported.
Refusing to verify challenges why verification is required; unable_to_verify_identity is for failed attempts.
Generic transfer cost question; nothing about topping up by bank transfer.
Transfer was stopped/declined with no beneficiary context; failed_transfer is also acceptable.
Repeated transfer errors with no beneficiary restriction mentioned.
Fee to get a physical card sits between get_physical_card and order_physical_card in this taxonomy.
'Reactivate my card' with no found-card context reads as activate_my_card, though the dataset files reactivation of a found card under card_linking.
Found a previously lost card and asks to use it again, which is the dataset's card_linking (re-link) sense; lost_or_stolen_card is for reporting loss.
Two-word fragment 'The card PIN?' is underspecified; dataset files PIN-for-physical-card under get_physical_card but change_pin is equally defensible.
Explicitly asks why a transfer is still pending.
Question is whether a specific card brand (Amex) can be used, i.e. supported cards, not how to top up by card.
Generic how-long question; no balance problem reported.
Asks whether SWIFT transfers are supported; no fee is mentioned.
Asks how long a UK transfer will take; nothing about a balance not updating.
Reactivating a found card is the dataset's card_linking sense, but activate_my_card is a defensible literal reading.
'Transfer wasn't allowed' is a declined transfer; beneficiary_not_allowed is plausible but the beneficiary is not mentioned.
Card top-up money disappeared, a failed top-up, not a how-to question.
Overcharged for ATM withdrawal; exchange rate is not mentioned.
The question is what an unexplained $1 charge is for; pending status is incidental.
General fraud-protection question that no intent covers; verify_my_identity has no support in the text and compromised_card is only the nearest fit.
Asks whether SWIFT transfers can be used; no fee is mentioned.
Charges for receiving money maps to the inbound-transfer fee intent, but receiving_money is also defensible.
Asks about additional cost of an ATM withdrawal abroad; exchange rate is not raised.
Asks what rate applies at foreign ATMs with no complaint; exchange_rate fits, but the ATM-specific rate intent is defensible.
Setting the PIN of a new physical card is filed under get_physical_card in this dataset, but change_pin is a fair literal reading.
Asks about using American Express to fund the account, i.e. card support, not the top-up procedure.
Generic how-long question; recipient non-receipt is not claimed.
Transfer errors out as not possible; no beneficiary restriction mentioned.
Asks whether verification is required before using the account, the dataset's why_verify_identity sense, not how to verify.
Could not use card in a store fits declined_card_payment and card_not_working equally.
Asking to have the card sent is an order request, but get_physical_card is equally defensible.
How long until money arrives is a timing question; no non-receipt is reported.
Wants to change currency, i.e. exchange; fiat_currency_support is about supported currencies.
Card top-up did not credit the account; not a how-to-top-up question.
Card is stuck in the ATM and the user wants it back; PIN mistyping is only the cause.
'My payment was stopped' most naturally means declined, but reverted is possible and the text is too thin to be sure.
Generic complaint about the exchange rate; no card payment is mentioned.
Reactivating a found card is the dataset's card_linking sense, but activate_my_card is a defensible literal reading.
